title: "Zero-shot Learning"
description: "Learning to recognize or perform tasks for classes or situations without task-specific labeled examples."
term: "Zero-shot Learning"
letter: "Z"
category: "Machine Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Zero-shot learning aims to make predictions for a class or task without
training on labeled examples of that exact class or task.

## Technical explanation

Methods transfer information from seen classes to unseen ones using semantic
attributes, text descriptions, pretrained representations, or generative
models. The model relies on relationships learned elsewhere; evaluation must
separate training classes from unseen test classes according to the intended
setting. Generalized zero-shot learning also evaluates performance on both
seen and unseen classes.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

It can extend models to new categories when labeled data is scarce or
expensive. Claims of zero-shot performance depend on carefully defined data
separation and may be affected by pretraining overlap or label leakage.

## How it works

Train or pretrain representations that connect inputs to semantic descriptions
or attributes. At inference, compare a new input with candidate class
representations or condition a model on a task description. Validate with
unseen examples and an explicit candidate set.

## Practical example

A vision-language model can rank candidate descriptions for an image class
that had no examples in the task-specific dataset. Evaluate on classes held
out from task training and report the prompts or text descriptions used.

## Common misconceptions

- Zero-shot means no task-specific labeled examples, not no prior training or
  knowledge.
- Zero-shot learning and zero-shot classification overlap, but the latter
  specifically describes assigning labels to inputs.
